h1: Premiere Pro alternative for Mac and Windows: edit, grade, mix
lead: FilmKoja is a Premiere Pro alternative for Mac and Windows, with Source and Program Monitors, a multitrack timeline, color correction and an audio mixer. You bring sequences over from Premiere Pro via XML or AAF. Try the app free for 3 days with your own footage.
highlights: Import via FCP XML, AAF, OTIO

features.title: Monitors, bins and multitrack timeline
features.text: You work with Source and Program Monitors, bins with thumbnails and a multitrack timeline with source patching and track targeting, sync lock and linked selection. There’s also multicam, nesting, colored markers (exportable as CSV) and undo with no step limit. In the keyboard shortcut editor you choose the standard layout of professional editing apps or set up your own shortcuts.

features.title: 3-point editing and trimming
features.text: You set In and Out points in the Source Monitor and insert or overwrite onto the patched tracks with a keyboard shortcut. There’s also Ripple, Roll, Slip, Slide, Rate Stretch and Razor, plus a Trim Monitor that shows both sides of the edit. With dynamic trimming you trim with J, K and L right during playback.

features.title: Color correction with scopes
features.text: You get basic correction, eight creative looks, RGB and hue curves, color wheels for shadows, midtones and highlights, HSL secondaries and vignette. Processing happens in linear light with 32-bit floating point. Waveform and vectorscope measure the final graded image, and you can use LUTs too.

features.title: Keyframes with speed graph
features.text: You animate position, scale, rotation, anchor point and opacity on every clip, plus 26 blend modes. Keyframes can be linear, Bezier, hold or eased, and each property has its own lane with value and speed graphs. For elaborate motion graphics there’s [EffectKoja](/software/effect-koja).

features.title: Audio to EBU R128
features.text: FilmKoja measures loudness (momentary, short-term, integrated) and true peak according to ITU-R BS.1770 and EBU R128. There are also clip effects like parametric EQ, dynamics, limiter, reverb, DeNoise and DeHummer, plus a track mixer with five insert slots per track, sends, submixes and automation. For bigger audio projects there’s [SoundKoja](/software/sound-koja).

features.title: Export in the background
features.text: Export as H.264 MP4 with AAC, as ProRes 422 HQ, as DNxHR in MOV or MXF, as a PNG sequence, animated GIF or WAV. Export runs as a background job with a progress bar, so you can keep editing in the meantime. Your Mac’s hardware encoder can handle H.264 and H.265.

features.title: Titles and subtitles
features.text: You design titles with an OpenType text engine including kerning, ligatures and bidirectional text, and there are Type, Shape and Pen tools right in the Program Monitor. You import and export subtitles as SRT, WebVTT or SCC with frame-accurate timing. If you like, you burn them into the picture on export.

features.title: Protection against data loss
features.text: FilmKoja saves atomically, keeps several automatic backup versions and writes a recovery log about one second after every change. So after a crash or power cut, you get unsaved changes back.

switching.title: Switching from Premiere Pro to FilmKoja on your Mac or PC
paragraphs: The basic principle stays the same: Source and Program Monitors, bins and a multitrack timeline with source patching and track targeting. You set In and Out points, insert or overwrite, and trim with Ripple and Roll or dynamically with J, K and L. In the keyboard shortcut editor you choose the standard layout of professional editing apps, and it shows you conflicts right away.

You bring Premiere projects over via XML or AAF; FilmKoja doesn’t open .prproj files directly. So export your sequence from Premiere Pro as Final Cut Pro XML or AAF and import it into FilmKoja, which also reads FCPXML, OpenTimelineIO, EDL and OMF. You open your media files directly, such as MP4 or MOV with H.264, HEVC or ProRes, and MXF with DNxHR. Check effects and color corrections carefully after importing, because interchange formats don’t carry every setting.

Good to know: there are no plugins (VST3, Audio Units, OpenFX), no camera RAW and no AV1 export. You export H.265 via your Mac’s hardware encoder in 8-bit SDR. Color correction and export rendering run on the CPU, which slows things down with heavy footage. There are hardly any AI features. FilmKoja is in active development: you get updates and new features automatically and free of charge.

How to test in 3 days: download the Kojalytics Launcher, install FilmKoja and import a sequence from a real project, ideally with original files from your camera or smartphone. Edit, grade and mix a short piece and export it in your target format. Then decide: €19.99 a month for all 13 apps, which you can [cancel](/kuendigen) online any time, or €79 once. The guide [Canceling your Adobe subscription](/ratgeber/adobe-abo-kuendigen) explains how to end a running Adobe subscription.

faq.q: Is FilmKoja a full Premiere Pro alternative?
faq.a: For many projects, yes: editing, trimming, multicam, color correction, keyframes, titles, subtitles, audio mixing and export are included. Not included are, among other things, plugins, camera RAW and opening .prproj files directly. FilmKoja is in active development, and you get updates free of charge. So test FilmKoja with your own footage before you commit.

faq.q: Can I open my Premiere Pro projects in FilmKoja?
faq.a: Not directly: you bring Premiere projects over via XML or AAF; FilmKoja doesn’t open .prproj files. Export the sequence from Premiere Pro as Final Cut Pro XML or AAF and import it into FilmKoja, which also reads FCPXML, OpenTimelineIO, EDL and OMF. You open media files like MP4, MOV and MXF with H.264, HEVC, ProRes or DNxHR directly; camera RAW isn’t supported.

faq.q: Which formats does FilmKoja export to?
faq.a: FilmKoja exports H.264 as MP4 with AAC audio, Apple ProRes 422 HQ and Motion JPEG as QuickTime, and DNxHR, ProRes or H.264 in MXF, plus PNG sequences, animated GIFs and WAV. You export H.265 via your Mac’s hardware encoder (8-bit, SDR), but not AV1. Export runs in the background, so you can keep editing in the meantime.

faq.q: How much does FilmKoja cost compared to Premiere Pro?
faq.a: Adobe Premiere (formerly Premiere Pro) costs €25.99 a month incl. VAT as a single app on an annual plan paid monthly, and if you cancel after 14 days, you pay 50% of the remaining contract value. After 3 free trial days, FilmKoja costs €19.99 a month, and that includes all 13 Koja apps. You can cancel online any time with no fee, or pay €79 once as a one-time purchase; both cover up to 3 devices. You’ll find all the details under [Pricing](/software#preise).

faq.q: Can I get Premiere Pro without a subscription?
faq.a: No. Adobe only offers Premiere as a subscription, either monthly or as an annual plan paid monthly or upfront, and annual plans renew automatically unless you cancel. For FilmKoja, you can pay €79 once instead and keep your license, with no subscription. You’ll find more alternatives to Adobe apps in the guide [Adobe alternatives for the Mac](/ratgeber/adobe-alternative-mac).

faq.q: Does FilmKoja work without internet and without an account?
faq.a: Yes. You don’t need an account, and after download and activation FilmKoja runs offline on your Mac or PC. The app decodes video with your Mac’s hardware (VideoToolbox); color correction and export rendering run on the CPU and can slow down with heavy footage. FilmKoja runs on macOS and Windows; there’s no web version.
